title: Netflix's I Will Find You Garners Massive Viewership but Mixed Reviews Despite Harlan Coben Adaptation
text:
I Will Find You, Netflix's new Harlan Coben thriller, has become the platform's biggest original debut of the year yet faces divided critical and audience reception with scores hovering around 60-66%. The eight-episode miniseries explores a father's quest to prove his innocence in his son's murder, starring Britt Lower. Despite strong viewership, reviews highlight uneven execution, from praise for its suspense to criticism of acting and dialogue. Additional entertainment news covers updates on Avengers: Endgame, The Angry Birds Movie 3, and more.
The new Harlan Coben suspense series I Will Find You has achieved massive viewership on Netflix but faces mixed critical and audience reactions. The eight-episode miniseries holds a 62% Tomatometer score based on 29 critic reviews and a 66% audience score on the Popcornmeter from over 100 ratings.
These mediocre scores highlight a gap between the show's popularity and its reception. Although currently classified as fresh, it remains far from certified fresh status. Critic reviews vary, with one awarding three out of four stars and noting that thrills persist even when the plot becomes far-fetched. Another gave three out of five stars, describing the show as merely clinically efficient despite its absurd storyline.
Audience responses are similarly divided, ranging from praise for its mystery and writing to criticism of acting, dialogue, and plotting. The series centers on David Burroughs, a man imprisoned for his son's murder who uncovers evidence that the child may still be alive. Britt Lower portrays his sister-in-law Rachel, who brings forth crucial evidence. All episodes are currently streaming on Netflix.
